solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hole in the wall passers inched around (13, two words)

indicators.note: letters moved around are put in a different order, so the two words are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written: thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Pedestrians edge their way round a gap in a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole in the wall' is the British colloquial name for a street cash machine, a fitting thing for passers-by to inch around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine set into a building's outer wall is informally called a hole in the wall in Britain.

clue.text: Unadorned melodies from American company in wild antic (11, two words)

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters of antic run riot into a new order
the company and the American go inside the scrambled word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
US is the standard abbreviation for American
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Plain tunes come from a US firm in a crazy prank.
explanation.walkthrough: CANTUS FIRMI is the plural of cantus firmus, the fixed plainsong melody round which other parts are woven.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantus firmus is a plain pre-existing melody used as the basis of a polyphonic composition; the plural matches 'melodies'.

clue.text: Young salmon species, what angler takes in hand

blocks.note: sp. is the abbreviation for species
an angler holds a fishing rod

explanation.surface: A fisherman holds his rod while describing a kind of young salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprod is a dialect word for a salmon in its second year, a young fish.

clue.text: Sort of barbecue food to suspend over middle of pit

indicators.note: only the central letter of the following short word is kept

blocks.note: to suspend something is to hang it
the middle letter of the three-letter word

explanation.surface: Instructions for cooking: hang meat above a fire pit.
explanation.walkthrough: A hangi is the Maori way of cooking in an earth oven, a pit of heated stones, so the pit in the surface belongs to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangi names both the Maori earth-oven feast and the food cooked in it, a kind of outdoor barbecue.

clue.text: Extended bit of verse? Digital player replaces one in time

indicators.note: one item takes the place of another inside the word for time

blocks.note: a day is a period of time
a, the indefinite article, means one
the iPod is Apple's digital music player

explanation.surface: A music player swapped in to keep time with a long passage of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: a dipody is a double foot, so it is a metrical foot extended to twice its length.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a dipody is a unit of two metrical feet, so it is a stretched-out piece of verse rhythm.

clue.text: Labouring unpaid e.g. in the main unearths old coin (11, two words)

indicators.note: labouring words are worked over and knocked into a new shape
the reworked letters sit inside the word for the sea

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: Someone working for nothing finds an antique coin while digging.
explanation.walkthrough: The spade guinea was a George III gold guinea whose shield is spade-shaped, which suits the digging picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade guinea is a historical British gold coin, named for the spade-shaped shield on its reverse.

clue.text: Basket for clothes or bread on middle of tray

indicators.note: only the central letters of the following word are kept
in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so the bread comes first

blocks.note: pita is a flat bread
the two middle letters of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A basket carries either laundry or a loaf set on a tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitara is an Indian box or basket in which clothes are kept or carried.

clue.text: Not far from Edinburgh, eastern quarter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
west is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Directions to somewhere close to Edinburgh, in the east part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Edinburgh' is part of the definition: it marks the word as Scots, meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewest is a Scots adjective meaning near or close by, hence a word heard in Edinburgh.

clue.text: It's used for swabbing decks, that is after sticky stuff's lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it upside down, so its letters run bottom to top
the abbreviation comes behind the upturned piece

blocks.note: goo is sticky stuff, plus the 's
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A deckhand scrubs the ship once the tar has been prised up.
explanation.definitionFit: Soogie, or sujee, is nautical slang for the soapy mixture or cloth used to scrub ship's paintwork and decks.

clue.text: Travel railroads illegally, free and easy once on perches (11, three words)

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces are placed on top of the last one

blocks.note: to rid is to free
ethe is an obsolete word for easy; 'once' marks it as old
a rod and a perch are the same old unit of length

explanation.surface: Birds sitting relaxed and carefree on their perches.
explanation.walkthrough: To ride the rods was North American hobo slang for travelling clinging to the rods under a freight wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom described hobos stealing rides beneath railway cars, which is travelling the railroads without paying.

clue.text: Father moving left couple, damage past

indicators.note: in an across clue moving leftwards means reading from right to left

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Dad walks out on a couple, the harm now behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' is part of the definition, marking the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Appair is an obsolete form of impair, meaning to harm or damage, so it is damage in a bygone sense.

clue.text: Mature Pacific tree, green all round – a sudden change

indicators.note: the vegetable surrounds the other pieces entirely

blocks.note: something mature is ripe
the ti is a palm-like tree of the Pacific islands
a pea is a green vegetable, and pea green a colour

explanation.surface: A ripening tropical tree, ringed with greenery, suddenly alters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripetia is the term from Greek drama for an abrupt reversal of fortune in a plot.

clue.text: Key points absorbed by idiotic officers in retreat

indicators.note: the letters are swallowed up inside the following words
retreating means going backwards, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Foolish officers take in the main points while falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci, plural of focus, are central points of attention or importance.

clue.text: I'll yield to fool in character, one sharing lessons

indicators.note: yielding means giving up one's place to another item

blocks.note: the climate of something is its prevailing character or mood
taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A pupil admits stepping aside for a clown who's quite a character.
explanation.definitionFit: A classmate is a fellow pupil, someone who attends the same lessons.

clue.text: Cheese, round, in yellow wrapping? It's opened out to be studied

definitions.text: It's opened out to be studied

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the cheese reads backwards
the colour is wrapped around the turned cheese

blocks.note: feta is a Greek cheese
gold is a yellow colour

explanation.surface: A wheel of cheese in yellow foil, unwrapped for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; the definition follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatefold is an oversized page folded into a book or magazine that the reader unfolds to look at.

clue.text: Colourful bird to be sold in marketplace

indicators.note: the phrase for being sold is placed inside the marketplace word

blocks.note: tron is a Scots word for a marketplace or its public weighing beam
goods that go are sold, as in 'it went for a fiver'

explanation.surface: A brightly feathered bird is up for sale at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Trogons are tropical birds with vivid green, red and yellow plumage, the quetzal among them.

clue.text: Gratuity some received as handout

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters across the end of the first word, the second word, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A tip is partly taken as a charitable handout.
explanation.walkthrough: Dash is a West African word for a tip or gift, sometimes a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: In West African usage a dash is a small payment or present given for a service, a gratuity.

clue.text: Ruby performed turns making one shiver

indicators.note: turning the whole thing about makes it run backwards

blocks.note: ruby is a shade of red
did is the past of do, to perform

explanation.surface: A performer called Ruby does turns frightening enough to make you shiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruby' looks like a stage name and 'turns' like acts on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Didder is a dialect verb meaning to shiver or tremble with cold or fear.

clue.text: What's added to drink, dry, weak one with dash of soda in?

indicators.note: a dash is a small splash, so only the first letter of the mixer is used
the other pieces are placed inside the word for dry

blocks.note: TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry
W is the abbreviation for weak
the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bartender asks what goes in a dry, weak drink with a splash of soda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' is not a description of the drink: TT stands for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a strip of citrus peel dropped into a cocktail as a garnish.

clue.text: Singular, smart, unconventional

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
smart in the sense of quick or brisk, as in a smart pace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' and 'smart' look like a list of compliments, but each supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacy, or spacey, means odd or eccentric, as if not quite on this planet.

clue.text: Dandy in a party, one of seven turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning upward means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A fop appears at a gathering, one of a group of seven arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a very handsome young man, used loosely for a beau or fop.

clue.text: On our side, holding ring that's anything but impregnable

indicators.note: the first phrase holds the ring inside itself

blocks.note: pro means on the side of, and us means our people
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: An ally wearing a ring that offers no defence at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impregnable' suggests a fortress but here means not letting liquid through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something porous lets water and air pass through it, the opposite of being sealed or impenetrable.

clue.text: The old pool contribution to couple's honeymoon

indicators.note: the following words each contribute some of their letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the first letter of the second

explanation.surface: Friends chip into a kitty to pay for a couple's honeymoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' looks like a shared fund of money; it is a pool of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Plesh is Spenser's word for a pool or puddle, hence an old word for a pool.

clue.text: Litter disfigured lake in Peru

indicators.note: something disfigured is spoiled in shape, so the letters lose their order
the reshaped letters are placed inside the country code

blocks.note: PE is the international vehicle code for Peru
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rubbish spoils a lake in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' wants to be rubbish; it is the old carried chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A palkee, or palki, is an Indian palanquin, a covered chair carried on poles like a litter.

clue.text: Last course over after post-school education? If so, one's had enough (5, two words)

definitions.note: an extended description of the state, not a synonym

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round
the turned dessert follows the education abbreviation

blocks.note: FE is further education, study after leaving school
pud, short for pudding, is the final course of a meal

explanation.surface: Dinner is over at the college; whoever finishes pudding has eaten enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had enough' plays on being full after a meal, while fed up means bored and exasperated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fed up is to be weary of something and unwilling to tolerate more of it.

clue.text: Installed head of state admitting space (5, two words)

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the leader's name takes in a gap

blocks.note: the surname of Russia's president
a blank space between letters, which splits the name into two words

explanation.surface: A national leader is installed, taking in room for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'space' is literally the gap between words, so the name becomes a two-word phrase without any letter changing.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in equipment is to install it, so put in means installed.

clue.text: Final challenge for Balliol undergrad, maybe, to announce impending nuptials for last time

definitions.text: to announce impending nuptials for last time

blocks.note: Balliol is an Oxford college, so its undergraduate belongs to OU, Oxford University
a task is a challenge, and finals are the last university exams

explanation.surface: An Oxford student's last exam comes before a final wedding announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The role of 'Final' puzzled solvers; it seems to evoke Oxford finals. Outask is an old term for calling the marriage banns the third and last time.
explanation.definitionFit: To outask was to proclaim banns of marriage for the final time in church before a wedding.

clue.text: Star group exchanging parts, no longer equal in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Star group' suggests a band of celebrities but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Samen is an obsolete Scots form of same, meaning equal or identical.

clue.text: King's given over part of church for his consort's junior in rank

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the second

blocks.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to the king: in cards the knave, or jack, ranks just below the queen, the king's consort.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the knave ranks below the queen, so it is junior to the king's wife.

clue.text: Flat layout with outer bits for atelier

clue.text: Distinctive sound of mobile Girton 'fresher', not old
